f: Ishmeet Kaur Chaudhry is an Associate Professor at the Department of English Studies at Central University of Gujarat, Vadodara. In 2015, she was selected for The President of India’s In-residence Program at Rashtrapati Bhawan, New Delhi. Earth and Embers: South Asia in Verse (2026) is her latest co-edited anthology of poems.

f: Jeet Thayil is the author of five novels and five books of poetry, and the editor of The Penguin Book of Indian Poets (2022). His most recent novel is The Elsewhereans (2025). He has co-edited (with Pascalle Burton) For Gaza: Art Against Genocide (2026).

f: Joba Murmu is a Santali author and translator. Most recently, she has translated Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s novel Anandamath into Santali (2025). b: Josy Joseph is a writer-journalist and the founder of Confluence Media, a platform-agnostic investigative journalism outfit. Winner of several awards, including the Prem Bhatia Trust’s ‘India’s best political reporter’…
f: Josy Joseph is a writer-journalist and the founder of Confluence Media, a platform-agnostic investigative journalism outfit. He was the National Security Editor of The Hindu . He is the author of the award-winning A Feast of Vultures: The Hidden Business of Democracy in India (2016), The Silent Coup: A History of India’s Deep State (2021), and Birth of a Nation: The Twenty-One Days That Made India (2026).

f: Jyotsna Mohan is an award-winning journalist and author with nearly three decades of experience across television, print, and digital media. The book chronicles the extraordinary history of her family’s newspaper and its place in India’s freedom struggle and journalistic legacy. A columnist for Indian and international publications, she writes on contemporary issues and public affairs, and also hosts the podcast, Table Talk with Jo . In 2025, she received the Sanatan Puraskar for Literature.

b: K Srinath Reddy is the founder and past President of the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI; 2006-2022). Currently an Honorary Distinguished Professor at PHFI, he was Head of Cardiology at the AIIMS, the first…
f: K Srinath Reddy is the founder and past President of the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI; 2006-2022). He received the WHO Director General’s Award, the Luther Terry Medal, and the Queen Elizabeth Medal. He was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2005. He has published nearly 600 scientific papers and two books: Make Health in India: Reaching a Billion Plus (2019) and Pulse to Planet: Long Lifeline of Human Health (2023).

f: K Ullas Karanth was trained as an engineer, but pursued his passion for wildlife biology, getting his master’s degree at the University of Florida, USA (1988), and a doctorate from Mangalore University (1993). f: Kanupriya Dhingra is a book historian, writer, and translator. She studies urban reading cultures and the social life of books. f: Kanuru Sujatha Rao is a former Union Secretary of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. She has an MA from Delhi University and an MPA from Harvard University, USA. She was a Takemi Fellow and Gro Harlem Brundtland Senior Leadership Fellow at the Harvard School of Public Health, USA. f: Karthika Naïr is a poet, fabulist, playwright, and librettist. Award for Book of the Year (Fiction), and was highly commended at the 2016 Forward Prizes for Poetry; and Electric Birds of Pothakudi , illustrated by Joëlle Jolivet, which was awarded the 2023 Prix Felipé for ecological children’s literature, shortlisted for the 2023 Deutsch-Französischer Jugendliteraturpreis, and adapted into a dance production POTHAKUDI (2026) by choreographer Fouad Boussouf. b: Kashiana Singh is a TEDx speaker, poet, and author of five poetry collections, including Witching Hour (2024) and Dualities of Albireo (2025). Her poetry explores liminal spaces and thresholds of identity, migration,…
f: Kashiana Singh is a TEDx speaker, poet, and author of five poetry collections, including Witching Hour (2024) and Dualities of Albireo (2025). Her poetry explores liminal spaces and thresholds of identity, migration, memory, and belonging. She serves as President of the North Carolina Poetry Society, Managing Editor of Poets Reading the News , and Program Ambassador for the Matwaala Collective, championing diverse voices and nurturing vibrant literary communities.

f: Kashmira Rao is the Curator and Co-Lead of Indigenous Yatra, working with rural and Indigenous communities across India to explore grassroots storytelling, Indigenous knowledge systems, and cultural continuity. With a multidisciplinary background in design, entrepreneurship, folk arts, and eco-living products, she creates participatory experiences, games, and knowledge products that bring local voices and lived realities to the forefront. Her work focuses on making Indigenous knowledge accessible and relevant across generations through creative, immersive, and community-led approaches that celebrate culture, strengthen resilience, and keep traditional wisdom alive.

f: Kavi Yaga is the author of The Vanishings: Eight Stories (2026), selected as the Judge’s Choice of the George Garrett Fiction Prize. f: Kavita Krishna Meegama holds a Master’s in International Education and Human Development from The George Washington University, USA, and is currently pursuing a Doctorate in Hindu Studies at the Hindu University of America (HUA). f: Lakshmi Reddy, R has 30 years of teaching experience at the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) Hyderabad. f: Mohsin Nizam Ahmed Mirajkar is a seventh-generation sitar and tanpura maker from Miraj, Maharashtra, carrying forward a 300-year legacy of artisanal excellence. f: Mosyel Syelsaangthyel Khaling belongs to the Uipo (Khoibu) Naga community of Manipur. His wider interests include Uipo cultural identity, traditional knowledge, language-based community development, and transmitting linguistic and cultural heritage to younger generations. Through his continuing work on Uipo language and literature, he hopes to contribute to the preservation and revitalisation of a language that forms an essential part of his community’s identity and heritage.

f: Parul Sharma was raised in small-town India, absorbing its rhythms, contradictions, and social codes. Her latest novel The Missing Piece (2026), described by The Hindu as “A family novel with social bite”, explores the themes of exile, inheritance, and ancestral homes. An alumna of Mudra Institute of Communications, Ahmedabad (MICA), she worked in consumer insights for twenty years before committing to writing full-time. f: Ram Ramaswamy taught at the Jawaharlal Nehru University from 1986 till his retirement in 2018. Between 2011 and 2015 he was Vice Chancellor of the University of Hyderabad. Educated at Madras University, IIT Kanpur, and Princeton University, his research interests have largely been in the physical sciences. An elected Fellow of The World Academy of Sciences, the Indian National Science Academy, and the Indian Academy of Sciences, he served as President of the Indian Academy of Sciences from 2016 to 2018. D.D. Kosambi: One Life, Many Worlds (2026) is his first work of nonfiction.

f: Ramanan Laxminarayan is the founder and president of the One Health Trust, an academic, and senior researcher affiliated with several leading universities in the US. During the Obama Administration, he served on the U.S. President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology’s antimicrobial resistance working group and was appointed a voting member of the U.S. Presidential Advisory Council on Combating Antimicrobial Resistance. Bacteria to Buddha: How Cooperation Shaped Consciousness–and Makes Us Human (2026) is his latest book.

Her debut novel Corals Bloom Again (2026) draws on her childhood spent in East Africa.

f: S.Y. Quraishi joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1971 and as the 17th Chief Election Commissioner of India, he introduced major electoral reforms. He served on the Board of the International Institute of Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA), Stockholm and was appointed, along with Kofi Annan, as the Global Ambassador of Democracy in 2018. He has represented India in election observation missions worldwide. Featured in the Indian Express list of 100 Most Powerful Indians (2011, 2012), he has delivered major lectures at Oxford, Harvard, and Columbia. He is currently Chancellor Emeritus of IILM University, Gurgaon. India and I: A Hundred Memories, Not a Memoir (2026) is his latest book.

f: Sajjad Shahid is a civil engineer with a keen interest in history, culture, art, and architecture. A dedicated heritage activist, he is the Telangana State Convener of INTACH. He is a prolific writer and his columns and articles are published regularly in leading newspapers and journals. His area of expertise is the history and culture of the Deccan Sultanates with a focus on Dakhni language and literature. He is presently a consultant to the Aga Khan Foundation for the Qutb Shahi Heritage Park Restoration Project in Hyderabad, and a Trustee of H.E.H The Nizam’s Museum.

f: Sathya Saran was the editor of Femina for 12 years after which she chose to be a full-time author, part time teacher, and a columnist. He was invited to London, Frankfurt, Paris, and Vienna to present his poems. He was also invited by The Gateway Lit Fest in Mumbai (2024) and BBLF in Bengaluru (2026). He has received the prestigious Voice of Kolkata Award and Poetry Icon Award recently. In July 2026, he read his poems at the World Poetry Festival, Global Vision Summit, held in Athens, Greece.

f: Shezzi M is a former Chartered Accountant and Company Secretary. She is an E-RYT 500-certified yoga instructor with additional specialisations in Yin Yoga and Prenatal Yoga. Her work has a simple intention: to help people feel rooted in themselves while keeping their hearts open to the world around them. Her teaching reflects her belief that in an increasingly disconnected world, finding balance begins with coming home to ourselves.

f: Siddhartha Menon has worked in various capacities with schools run by the Krishnamurti Foundation India, for more than thirty years. He began writing poetry more seriously while working at a small rural school near Uttarkashi in the late 1990s, and his first book Woodpecker (2010) collects poems from this period. Subsequently, he has published four further collections. His poems have appeared in various journals and anthologies. He has been awarded the Vijay Nambisan Poetry Fellowship for 2026, and The Two Pits: New and Selected Poems (2026) is his latest book.

b: Siva Murugappan is a veteran General Surgeon with over 35 years of medical experience spanning both developing and developed healthcare systems. He currently serves as a General surgeon at the Chatham-Kent Health…
f: Siva Murugappan is a veteran General Surgeon with over 35 years of medical experience spanning both developing and developed healthcare systems. He currently serves as a General surgeon at the Chatham-Kent Health Alliance in Chatham, Ontario, Canada. In 2017, he survived a major ischemic stroke while working at an Ontario hospital. Following an intensive two-year rehabilitation process, he successfully returned to clinical practice, initially starting with minor surgeries and endoscopies. He co-authored the book Frontiers: The Journey of Two Surgeons Through Stroke (2024) with his wife Dr. Santhi Prema Priya Samy.

She is one of the 25 photographers featured in the Women in Photography-India project by ZIIP Foundation. She collaborates with grassroots organizations on visual projects. With a background in the development sector, she blends photography, research and writing to bring depth to narratives of underrepresented communities.

She has published books, translations, and research papers in linguistics and translation.

He also co-authored Pillars of Life: Magnificent Trees of the Western Ghats (2018) with his partner Divya Mudappa. Together, as scientists of the Nature Conservation Foundation, they now lead a programme to restore tropical rainforests of the Western Ghats.

f: Tariq Khan is the Officer-in-charge of the National Translation Mission. He has obtained MA, MPhil and PhD in Applied Linguistics from the Centre for Applied Linguistics and Translation Studies, University of Hyderabad. He serves as the editor of Translation Today and as Associate Editor of the Bibliography of Pragmatics Online (John Benjamins) and Springer Nature Social Sciences . He takes interest in psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics, writing systems, humour research, translation studies, and intercultural pragmatics. He has published in linguistics and translation studies and has edited lexical resources including Translation Equivalents in Indian languages for several academic disciplines.

f: Teresa Rehman is an award-winning journalist. She worked for India Today, Telegraph , and Tehelka before launching The Thumb Print which she edits currently. She received the WASH Media Awards 2009-2010, the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award for two consecutive years 2008-2009 and 2009-2010, the Laadli Media Award for Gender Sensitivity 2011, Sanskriti Award 2009 for Excellence in Journalism, and the Sarojini Naidu Prize 2007 by the Hunger Project for Best Reporting on Panchayati Raj. She is the author of The Mothers of Manipur: T welve Women who Made History (2017), Bulletproof: A Journalist’s Notebook on Reporting Conflict (2019) and Her Hajj Story: Travel Diaries of Women Pilgrims from Assam (2026).

f: Thingnam Anjulika Samom is an independent researcher and translator. She has translated many short stories and poems from Manipuri into English, and also edited Crafting The Word: Women’s Writings from Manipur (2019). A former journalist who also undertakes independent research and documentation work, she has contributed to various publications and has recently led an independent documentation of Manipuri women’s narratives of the Second World War.

f: Tongbram Amarjit Singh is a Manipuri poet, translator, visual artist, and cultural activist. He is currently the President of Sahitya Thoupang Lup, Imphal, and works as a Translation Officer at the Manipur Legislative Assembly Secretariat. ​His debut poetry collection Loubukki Manam (2013) won the 2018 Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puruskar and the Dharambir Literary Award. His second poetry book Imagi Keithel (2023) was honored with the Chingkhu Moirang Leima Kabirdas Mana (2024). He is the founder of the Loktak Folklore Museum and the programme manager for the Kalen Art Exhibition. He designs book covers, exhibits in prominent shows, and contributes feature articles and reviews to promote Manipuri literature.

f: Uma Magal is a documentary filmmaker, film educator, arts writer, and theatre practitioner whose career spans India, the U.S. and Ireland. Her documentary, Other Kohinoors, the Rocks of Hyderabad (2022) won over twenty international awards, and her documentary on Indian theatre The Players (2013) was broadcast nationally by NDTV. She published research articles in Asian Cinema Journal , a book Rasayana for Childcare: Joy of Herbs and Healing (2015), and was an arts journalist at The Hindu, Hans India , and Tehelka . She studied film and media at Temple University, Philadelphia, Jamia Millia Islamia, and taught at COMMITS, Bengaluru, University of Hyderabad, Annapurna Film School, San Francisco State, and Temple University.

f: Varala Anand is a poet, writer, film critic, documentary filmmaker, and cultural activist. A pioneer of the film society movement in northern Telangana, he helped establish several film societies and conceptualized the Film Bhavan in Karimnagar. His publications include Laya (1980), Maneru Teeram (1998), Maneru Galagala (2014), Merupu (2016), Manishi Lopala (2017), Aksharala Chelime (2018), Muktakalu (2020), Karachalanam(2025), and Triveni (2025). His translation of Gulzar’s Green Poems as Aakupacha Kavitalu (2019), won him the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2022. His anthology Irugu Porugu (2023) includes translations of poetry from 29 Indian languages, and his memoir Yaadon Ki Baraat (2024) represents literary exchange, cultural memory, and Telangana’s heritage.

f: Vasuki Shastry is an author and senior advisor on ESG, financial regulatory policy, strategic communications, and geopolitical risk for several public and private sector firms. He serves on the Advisory Council of Chatham House on the UK & The World Program, the Global Commemorations Committee of the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, and is a Trustee of the Institute of Human Rights and Business. He held senior positions at Standard Chartered Bank, London; International Monetary Fund (IMF), Washington D.C.; and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). His publications include Resurgent Indonesia (2018), Has Asia Lost it (2021), The Notorious ESG (2023), and Emerged Markets: The Global Economy’s Better Half (2026).

f: Veio Pou enjoys a slow life that gives him time to explore everyday narratives of humanity. He teaches literature and culture in the Department of English, University of Delhi. His debut novel, Waiting for the Dust to Settle (2020), won the 2021 Gordon Graham Prize for Naga Literature. The Renegade (2026) is a collection of short stories.

b: Vijaya Gopal holds a master’s degree in zoology and a PhD in life sciences. After a postdoctoral tenure in San Antonio, Texas, she returned to the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB). She was a visiting…
f: Vijaya Gopal holds a master’s degree in zoology and a PhD in life sciences. After a postdoctoral tenure in San Antonio, Texas, she returned to the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB). She was a visiting scientist at the Curie Institute (France), National Cancer Institute (USA), National Institute of Genetics (Japan), and Northwestern University (USA); a research grants reviewer for The World Academy of Sciences, Italy; and an executive member of the State Inter-University Centre of Excellence in Bioinformatics, University of Kerala. She served as a scientific advisor to Intellectual Property India – Biotechnology and Microbiology. From Helix to Horizon is her first book.

f: Viji Krishnamoorthy was born in Ipoh, Perak, to a Tamil father and Hokkien Chinese mother. She spent her early school years in Kuala Lumpur and later in Madras, as it was then known, before completing her tertiary education in the UK. She previously worked as a freelance writer for several magazines. Her debut novel 912 Batu Road (2021) was longlisted for the Dublin Literary Award 2023. Her latest novel Agnès (2026) is a sweeping historical story set in Penang against the backdrop of the Second World War and the Malayan Emergency, exploring questions of identity, belonging, injustice, love and resilience. She currently lives in Kuala Lumpur.

f: Vivek Narayanan is a 2026 Guggenheim Fellow in Poetry. His other honours include fellowships from the Radcliffe Institute and the New York Public Library. His books of poems include After (2022) and The Kuruntokai and its Mirror (2024). His work has appeared in many venues, including Poetry , The Paris Review , and The Penguin Book of the Prose Poem . He teaches in the MFA Poetry programme at George Mason University, USA.

b: Wahajullah Khan is a researcher specialising in the tangible and intangible heritage of the Deccan. With seven years of experience, his work focuses on the Sultanate period, military traditions and urban heritage. He…
f: Wahajullah Khan is a researcher specialising in the tangible and intangible heritage of the Deccan. With seven years of experience, his work focuses on the Sultanate period, military traditions and urban heritage. He has curated exhibitions including ‘Charminar-444’ and ‘The Musi and the Evolution of Hyderabad’, and is the organising co-founder of Shehr Festival. His fieldwork spans heritage documentation, surveys, and archival research across the Deccan. He recently co-led a digitisation programme at GITAM University and authored A Brief History of the Musi River (2026). His work advocates the preservation and wider appreciation of the Deccan’s shared heritage.

f: Yumnam Sapha Wangam Apanthoi M is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Fine Arts, Manipur University. He is the illustrator of two books: And That is Why: Manipuri Myths Retold (2021) and Feathers, Fools and Farts: Manipuri Folktales Retold (2023). His interests extend beyond art practice to include folklore, material culture, and visual arts. He has participated in numerous exhibitions and workshops organized by Lalit Kala Akademi and State Kala Akademi at regional, national, and international levels. He has received several awards and honors from the Government of Manipur and art societies of India, including the Manipur State Kala Akademi Award in 2006.
